mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 4% signals supply-side disruptions in an otherwise tight labor market, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate inflationary pressures and defensive sector outperformance.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts liquidity and reduces risk premia, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 3.5% signals a tight labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate pricing power, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is above 3% for three consecutive months signals a buildup of precautionary savings amid inflation, which dampens near-term consumption and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly increase in real GDP (GDPC1) of at least 2% for three consecutive quarters signals a robust demand-driven expansion, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 70% of quarters where GDPC1 rises by at least 2% for three consecutive quarters.
